facts.text: Scottsboro was originally named Scottsville, briefly became Scott's Mill, then settled on Scottsboro in 1858.
The town’s founder, Robert T. Scott, built a grist mill, shingle factory, and lobbied the Memphis and Charleston Railroad to run through his property, sparking the town’s growth.
Scottsboro is the site of the Scottsboro Boys Museum and Cultural Center, which chronicles the landmark civil‑rights trials that put the town on the national stage.
The city’s Jackson County Court House was the venue for the 2004 dedication of a historical marker honoring the Scottsboro Boys’ struggle for justice.
Scottsboro’s economy shifted from agriculture and lumber to TVA‑influenced development after 1933, reshaping the region’s industrial path.
